topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the cancer biology lecture series and outlines the core learning outcomes for the course.

topics.label: Biological concepts of cancer development and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as a multi-step disruption of genetic regulation, cellular differentiation, and tissue architecture, and discuss approaches for studying these cellular disruptions.

topics.label: Mechanisms of tumour invasion, metastasis, and histological progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the processes of tumor invasion and metastasis, illustrating the histological progression from benign to malignant lesions using colorectal cancer.

topics.label: Tumour nomenclature, clinical hazards, and mechanisms of mortality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the standard naming conventions of tumors and the physiological mechanisms through which benign and malignant growths cause disease and death.

topics.label: Tumour incidence across humans and other animal species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the incidence and mortality patterns of tumors in human populations and compare them with tumor occurrence across other animal species.

topics.label: Clinical detection and cancer screening modalities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the principles, histological methods, and clinical limitations of population screening for early cancer detection.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarizing the learning outcomes and providing reminders for upcoming practical sessions.
